actions.investigated_summary: The hypothesis that employee lihua performed the 2024-05-10 customer-dataset export is not supported by the recorded evidence. Per the application log (E3), the export of dataset 'customers' (184112 rows) to /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz completed at 2024-05-10 01:03:40 under account=svc_export, immediately after a SCHEDULE trigger at 2024-05-09 23:55:01 for job=nightly_export, which matches the daily 23:55 schedule in /scheduler/jobs.conf (E4). The case README (E2) characterizes svc_export as a dedicated non-interactive service account used by scheduled jobs. lihua appears in the captured log only in two FAILED login attempts at 2024-05-10 01:47:11 and 01:47:59 from 198.51.100.44 (reason=password), ~44 minutes after the export completed, with no successful lihua session. Attribution therefore points to the scheduled nightly_export job running as svc_export, not lihua.
limitations: Delegated source scope labeled 'windows' but no Windows-derived evidence (Security 4624/4625, Sysmon, Prefetch, Amcache, ShimCache, registry) is present; evidence is Linux-style application/scheduler/README files.
No OS-level authentication or session logs captured; account attribution relies solely on the application log's self-reported account= field plus the README's characterization of svc_export.
The export artifact /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz is not present in the captured files; its existence and contents are asserted only by the log line.
All three captured files share identical mtime/ctime (1790594134); file-system timestamps do not independently corroborate the in-log event times.
lihua's activity is limited to two failed logins in the captured log; additional lihua activity on other hosts or outside the captured log range cannot be excluded.

actions.text: The 2024-05-10 customer-dataset export (184112 rows → /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz) was performed by the scheduled job nightly_export running under the dedicated non-interactive service account svc_export, not by employee lihua; lihua's only recorded activity in the captured log is two failed password logins from 198.51.100.44 at 2024-05-10 01:47:11 and 01:47:59, which occurred after the export completed and produced no successful session.

actions.attempted_resolution: Resolved in favor of the log-based attribution: the analyst's hypothesis that lihua performed the 2024-05-10 customer export is contradicted by E3, which records the export under account=svc_export immediately after a SCHEDULE trigger for job=nightly_export matching the daily 23:55 schedule in E4, and by E2, which identifies svc_export as the dedicated non-interactive service account used by scheduled jobs. lihua's only recorded activity is two failed password logins from 198.51.100.44 at 2024-05-10 01:47:11 and 01:47:59, ~44 minutes after the export completed, with no successful session.
actions.impact: The primary investigative premise (lihua as the exporter) is overturned; the actual actor per recorded evidence is the automated nightly_export job running as svc_export. Downstream conclusions, containment actions, and any attribution of the export to lihua must be retracted or reframed.
actions.limitation: Resolution rests on application-layer evidence only (E3 account= field, E4 schedule, E2 account description). No OS-level session/credential logs are captured to independently confirm which principal executed the process, and the export artifact itself was not captured; a residual (unproven) possibility remains that the application log's account= field was spoofed or that the scheduled job was abused.

actions.capability_basis: Application-layer attribution established from the export log's account= field (E3), the scheduler definition for nightly_export (E4), and the README's characterization of svc_export as a dedicated non-interactive service account (E2).
actions.limitation: No OS-level authentication/session evidence (Windows Security 4624/4625 or Linux auth.log), no credential/privilege review of svc_export, no capture of the export artifact /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz, and no network-egress correlation are available; the delegated 'windows' scope produced no Windows-derived artifacts. Attribution is therefore application-log-only and not independently corroborated.

actions.text: Obtain the OS-level authentication/session log covering 2024-05-10 00:00–02:00 (Windows Security 4624/4625 or Linux auth.log) to independently confirm which principal executed the export process and to enumerate the full history of lihua's login attempts from 198.51.100.44.

Capture the export artifact /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz (or its hash, size, and mtime) to verify the export actually completed and to bound the data exfiltrated (184112 rows of the 'customers' dataset).

Review the credentials, privileges, and scope of access of svc_export, along with prior nightly_export runs, to establish whether the 2024-05-10 export is routine or anomalous (e.g., unusually large row count, unexpected destination, credential reuse, or job tampering).

Correlate network egress logs for 2024-05-09 23:55 – 2024-05-10 02:00 to determine whether /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz was transferred off-host, and whether 198.51.100.44 corresponds to a known location for lihua.

The export was triggered by the scheduled job 'nightly_export' (SCHEDULE event at 2024-05-09 23:55:01), consistent with the daily 23:55 schedule defined in /scheduler/jobs.conf.
The exported dataset was 'customers' with 184112 rows, written to /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz, and completed successfully in 18 seconds at 2024-05-10 01:03:40.

lihua attempted two logins on 2024-05-10 at 01:47:11 and 01:47:59 from IP 198.51.100.44, both FAILED (reason=password), ~44 minutes after the export completed; no successful lihua session appears in the captured log.

The recorded evidence does not corroborate the analyst's hypothesis that lihua performed the export; the temporal ordering (export completed before lihua's failed logins) and account attribution both point to the automated svc_export job as the actor.

lihua's failed logins at 01:47 from 198.51.100.44 may reflect a separate attempt (guessing/brute-forcing the password or a legitimate mistyped login) and warrant separate review, but they did not result in an export per the available log.
